quest.title: Prophets of Pop
quest.description: You meet a musician in Natlan named Milu Nui, but he appears to have run into some trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You could try gathering some sound samples...

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Sounds...? Oh, do you mean to say that we could sample the sounds of nature and use them directly in the songs?

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Hmm... That does sound like a good idea. Yes, very good indeed! See, I knew you were a sharp shovel! Come on, let's get going!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, you're not bringing anything with you?

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Of course not. Or are you expecting me to drag a gramophone around out there?

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we're just going to see what sorts of sounds we can use.

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: A duck flapping its wings, for instance, or the splash made as a Koholasaurus hits the water, or the rumbling footsteps of a Tepetlisaurus walking...

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Once we've selected out targets, I'll make the preparations to take those sound samples... but that's all for later.

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: As for the here and now, let's head out — time's a-wasting!

talks.objective: Go gather materials with Milu Nui

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Look at those birds, listen to their cries! My, oh my, if those wouldn't make excellent material for my next work!

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Still, things could get pretty one-note if we only recorded a few of them. If we could find a whole flock and record the sound of their collective calls...

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Hang on, that's a Koholasaurus just up ahead. You hear how it scratches the stone with its claws?

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Koholasaurs are the sensitive sort, so let's not get too close. I'll get some professionals from our tribe to gather what I need afterward — if anyone can pull this off, it'd be them.

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Oh, ho... warriors testing themselves against one another. Good, good, the sounds of battle are lovely indeed...

dialogues.speaker: Angry Tribal Warrior
dialogues.text: Oi! What're you skulking about for? You here for a fight?

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: We're just... gathering materials...

dialogues.speaker: Angry Tribal Warrior
dialogues.text: Gathering? Well, I'll show you "gathering"!

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: #H—Help! {NICKNAME}, stop him!

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: #Phew! You're quite the dab hand yourself, aren't you, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: You seem good at persuading the more agitated types...

choices.text: That wasn't even my full power.

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: I could tell. In every possible aspect... it is quite obvious.

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: Well, that was quite the adventure, but either way, I've selected plenty of sounds to sample.

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: After just a bit of prep work, I'll be able to officially start recording the audio...

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: Hmm... We should start with the "sounds of battle"...

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: Wait, no. That's not a good place to begin. We should open up with something more normal...

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: That's very modest of you. Thank you, in any case.

talks.objective: Seek customer feedback in the shop

dialogues.speaker: Haloa Nui
dialogues.text: Ooh, a new record! The baby Saurian's gonna love this!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about Milu Nui's music...

dialogues.speaker: Haloa Nui
dialogues.text: I love Uncle Milu's songs — and really, the baby Saurian we have back home loves them more than I do!

dialogues.speaker: Haloa Nui
dialogues.text: Whenever it gets too rowdy, Mom plays one of his songs, and then it quiets down real quick.

dialogues.speaker: Haloa Nui
dialogues.text: Hmm... Those songs are super long, though. I can barely remember the lyrics, let alone sing 'em for it...

dialogues.speaker: Haloa Nui
dialogues.text: Hehe, if he could write some songs with fewer lyrics, I'd be able to sing them every day for that kid's listening pleasure!

talks.objective: Seek customer feedback in the shop

dialogues.speaker: Mahina Nui
dialogues.text: Mr. Milu's released a new record! Should I buy it or not...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about Milu Nui's music...

dialogues.speaker: Mahina Nui
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh, he's great! Haloa and the baby Saurian love it.

dialogues.speaker: Mahina Nui
dialogues.text: Every time they get all rowdy and stubborn and don't wanna sleep, I'll play them Mr. Milu's "Spring-Day Song."

dialogues.speaker: Mahina Nui
dialogues.text: As soon as they hear it, they're asleep in no time — voila, sweet dreams, see you tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Mahina Nui
dialogues.text: Still, though... Haloa has been saying that she'd prefer something a bit more intense.

dialogues.speaker: Mahina Nui
dialogues.text: If Mr. Milu could come up with a couple of tunes with a bit more energy, I'm sure she'd have more fun with 'em.

talks.objective: Seek customer feedback in the shop

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: ...Milu's style is the same as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about Milu Nui's music...

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh, I love his style of composition. I listen to his songs after work. Really helps me relax.

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: But if you asked me personally, I'd call his lyrics... a bit, well, overly complex.

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: *sigh* I wish he'd make a record without lyrics, y'know? Only instrumental tracks.

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: How did it go? Did they have any feedback?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've heard these opinions...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You convey the customer feedback to Milu Nui...

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: A—Ah. Is that how things are? Thank you, the feedback is quite valuable. Let me see what I can change...

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Still, from the sound of it... aren't they all treating my records like kids' songs!?

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: ...No, no, all the more reason to make some changes... Still, where do I begin?

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Seriously, there's no getting through to Pakaa... He doesn't understand my musical ideals at all!

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: Hmm? You're a... traveler? Greetings. Call me Milu Nui. I'm a musician.

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: If you've been to Xochicuicatl Records, you'll have seen my records in the pop music section.

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: They contain all that I understand of "pop" itself.

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: It's just that Pakaa doesn't understand me at all, and insists that my music resembles "kiddy music" more than it does "pop."

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: And no matter what I say, he wants my records placed in the children's section!

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: I mean, yes, children do like my songs, and some parents do buy them as gifts for their kids...

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: But in truth, children are the keenest listeners! And there's a lot of them in the tribe anyhow...

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: So if my records are so popular amongst the kids, I should have a spot in the pop section!

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: Right? Hmph! I knew Pakaa was just being his usual ignorant self. But no more! Once I'm done writing this new song, he'll have no choice but to admit how impressed he is!

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: Not that I trust his taste in music anymore, though... Anyway, traveler, how familiar would you call yourself with music?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Uhh...

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: Do you play an instrument? It's fine if you just sing or hum!

choices.text: I'm as musically versatile as they come.

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: Awesome! In that case, I'm sure you'll understand my philosophy of music!

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: Someone like you is exactly who I need if I'm to create this all-new jam.

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: Don't worry, I'll have a most ample reward ready — it'll be well worth your while.

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: Alright then. Just use your intuition, and tell me — what should I do first to create an excellent piece of music?

response.speaker: Milu Nui
response.text: No matter! Only someone like you can truly enjoy music from the heart. I'm sure your judgment will be all the more objective and fair for it.

choices.text: And what are these musical ideals you speak of?

dialogues.speaker: Haloa Nui
dialogues.text: Hehe, if he could write some songs with fewer lyrics, I'd be able to sing them every day for that kid's listening pleasure!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should hear from customers first.

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Well, that... I don't disagree, and I've actually made some inquiries myself...

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: But it feels like they just default to pleasantries when they see me, so I never get to hear their honest opinions.

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, could you help me ask around instead?

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: I imagine they'll... feel more comfortable being honest with you.

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Pop... What is pop, anyway? Goodness...

dialogues.speaker: Mahina Nui
dialogues.text: If Mr. Milu could come up with a couple of tunes with a bit more energy, I'm sure she'd have more fun with 'em.

dialogues.speaker: Tirda
dialogues.text: *sigh* I wish he'd make a record without lyrics, y'know? Only instrumental tracks.

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Pop... *sigh* What is pop, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And how are you going with your musical ideals?

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}, a pleasure to see you again! As for my musical ideals, I can only say that... I'm hard at work seeking a breakthrough.

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: *sigh* But what sort of "pop" is everyone looking for, really? And how is "pop" supposed to feel?

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: #I know you're someone who appreciates music, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: So please, would you mind giving me some more suggestions based on your intuition? What should I do first to create an excellent piece of music?

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Phew! Alright, this is the spot. Look at the nature all around us! Bask in its perfection!

dialogues.speaker: Milu Nui
dialogues.text: Come, let us walk about. Surely, there must be some interesting audio for us to sample!
